Question: Is Nvidia stock a good buy?
Answer: Want an incredible stat? Nvidia’s stock price is now worth more in terms of market capitalisation than the Chinese and Hong Kong stock markets combined! It is also bigger than some European markets. US big tech has also doubled its size relative to the US stock market, per Schroders's graphic. I won’t give tips on individual stocks. Nvidia might be the future due to AI, or maybe it won’t be. However, technology is the kind of area where firms can quickly get superseded by superior alternatives. We saw that during the late 90s. Most tech firms went to zero, and a few got incredibly big. It wasn’t easy to find out which of those firms, in advance of time, would get big. We might see something similar in the future. So, diversifying beyond technology stocks is very important.

Question: What is your proof for, "If you work harder than most people you will be more successful than most people"?
Answer: There is no evidence that everybody who works harder will become more successful, because chance/randomness/luck plays a role. There is evidence that if you take a large sample, more hardworking and conscientious people tend to be more successful. This can be found in income data: But it goes beyond income. People who are more hard-working and conscientious are more likely to be successful in other domains because they: The last two points, however, show that hard work is most effective when it is combined with: Being hard-working in one domain, giving up and starting a new idea, and then doing the same again isn’t usually very effective. You have to work hard on the right things, which is working smart, but the harder you work, the easier it is to know how to work smart above a certain age. Working smart at 21, straight out of university, doesn’t work as well as working smart at 31 or 41 with much more experience and potentially financial resources on your side! Finally, it would be best to remember that supply and demand laws exist here. Many people are willing to work hard for a short period, but few are willing to do it for a decade or longer. You only have to work 5%-10% harder than most of your competitors for a decade to get real advantages, as these things compound, but it is incredible how many people try to work 50% harder and then give up! Even fewer are prepared to take many risks, especially if taking such risks makes them unpopular in their industry or wider society. Many traditionally hard-working and conscientious people can be pretty risk-averse. So, adding risk-taking to the hard and smart working equation works very well.
